Essential for converting ion impacts to measurable electrical signals. Common types include electron multipliers, photomultipliers, and Faraday cups. Required in all systems.
Critical for maintaining low pressure environment needed for ion flight paths. Includes pumps and chambers. Essential for proper operation and ion trajectory control.
Necessary for introducing samples to the ion source. Can be direct insertion probes, chromatography interfaces, or direct infusion - varies by application but always present.
Required for signal processing, data collection and spectrum generation. Modern systems are computerized but the electronics for signal conversion are fundamental components.
Provides various voltages needed for ion source, analyzer, and detector operation. Critical for generating electric fields but often integrated into other components.
Manages timing, voltages, and operational parameters. Essential for coordinated operation of all subsystems but may be distributed across other components.
